hero.heading: EMDR therapy
hero.intro: Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing is a structured therapy that helps the brain process distressing memories, so they feel less present and less charged.
hero.evidenceNote: Recommended for PTSD by the American Psychological Association and the World Health Organization.
hero.tileSummary: A structured, research-backed method for processing distressing memories.

image.alt: Two chairs by a window in soft daylight

whoItHelps.heading: EMDR may help if you live with
items: Panic or startle responses tied to past events
The effects of an abusive relationship
Childhood experiences that still shape how you feel

steps.title: History & planning
steps.body: We map what you want to work on, and in what order.

steps.title: Preparation
steps.body: You learn grounding skills to use in and between sessions.

steps.title: Processing
steps.body: Short sets of eye movements or taps while you hold a memory in mind.

steps.title: Integration
steps.body: We check what has shifted and close each session steady.

items.question: Do I have to describe the memory in detail?
items.answer: No. EMDR does not require you to talk through every detail. You stay in control of what you share.

items.question: How many sessions will I need?
items.answer: It depends on your history and goals. Your clinician will give you an estimate after the assessment.

items.question: Can EMDR be done online?
items.answer: Yes. Online EMDR uses on-screen movement or self-tapping and follows the same structure.
